diggin; on the Prairie Wind eh?

I keep going back and forth on it, I can't seem to make up my mind whether it is merely good, brilliant, or a relatively poor effort with two or three stand out tracks that really raise the level of the album as a whole.

I think "It's a Dream", "Falling Off The Face Of The Earth", "When God Made Me" and "This Old Guitar" are brilliant, ESPECIALLY "It's A Dream".

I think "He Was The King" and "Here For You" are not so good.

The title track, "Far From Home" and "No Wonder" I think are interesting, but flawed.

"The Painter" is pleasant but forgettable.

I understand he wrote the album in a week and recorded it as the songs came.  In retrospect I have to wonder whether a little more time and thought might have fixed up some of those tunes.

However, I like the sound of the album so I can't seem to make up my mind about it.

I dunno.

John Coltrane - One Down, On Up: Live At The Half Note

This is a new two-CD* set of performances recorded at the Half Note club in NYC in 1965 (one in March, one in May). The title track has been circulated before, but in amateur/bootleg versions; this is the first offical release of this material, and it's heavy. It could be considered "transitional" material, between the "classic" Coltrane quartet's music and the later more "out" Coltrane music.
